Aisha Khan: Quick proposal for autoscaler changes for spot-backed inference pools — want feedback before I open a PR. TL;DR: add a scale-safety margin, decouple surge cap from target replicas, and introduce a fast-path fallback to dedicated when interruption risk spikes.

Leo: do you have numbers for how often we see interruption bursts that matter?

Aisha Khan: last 90 days, APAC spot eviction bursts roughly 3x/week where interruption probability > 20% for 10–30m windows. Cost-wise we save ~65% on spot vs dedicated but tail latency and throttling during bursts cause user-visible errors.

Mateo: +1 for decoupling surge cap. Right now we block scale-outs because of a global surge limit and it causes request queuing that trips request timeouts.

Jin: curious about the safety margin idea — what's the algorithm?

Aisha Khan: Safety margin = max(ceil(0.15 * desired_replicas), 1) reserved as soft headroom. Autoscaler computes desired_replicas from queued work + latency SLO. We allocate desired_replicas + safety_margin but mark safety slots as spot_hedged: they must land on on-demand or dedicated if spot provisioning latency>threshold or interruption_risk>threshold.

Priya: so safety slots are effectively hot standby but cheaper than fully-reserved? how do we avoid paying too much?

Aisha Khan: we only fill safety slots if spot capacity is available within X sec (configurable; default 45s). If spot doesn't satisfy within that window, fallback routes provisioning requests to dedicated pool with best-effort cost center. We'll evaporate safety slots after cooldown if not used.

DevOps Bot: [autoscaler] detected surge in spot interrupts in ap-southeast-1; current interrupt_prob=0.27; suggested action: activate safety_margin and failover route.

Sam: can we simulate the billing delta? I'd like a worst-case monthly cost estimate if we fall back often.

Mateo: I ran a quick sim — assuming 30% of safety slots fall back to dedicated for 20m windows, cost increase is ~8–12% but p99 tail latency drops by ~40% and failed requests drop 75%.

Jin: what about cooldown behavior? we need to avoid oscillation if spot returns quickly.

Aisha Khan: propose two cooldowns: scale-out cool = 90s, but safety-fallback cooldown = 10m where fallback dedicated replicas remain for at least that period to stabilize. For scale-down we use conservative window 15m to avoid thrash.

Priya: what about mixed-capacity placement preferences? i.e., prefer pools with lower interruption history first?

Aisha Khan: yes. Placement policy: sort candidate pools by (1) historical interrupt_rate (30d EWMA), (2) provisioning latency, (3) cost multiplier. Weighted scoring. We prefer multi-region spread when possible for critical workloads.

Leo: and surge controls? current global surge cap is causing long queues as Mateo said.

Aisha Khan: change to tiered surge caps: per-customer cap (small), per-region cap (medium), global emergency cap (larger) — but emergency cap has a circuit breaker that trips if endpoint error rate > 2% or interrupt_prob > 0.3. Circuit breaker will auto-shed non-critical routes.

Sam: how will this interact with rollout policies? canary jobs might get starved if we divert capacity to safety slots.

Aisha Khan: rollout policy update: mark canaries as lower priority in spot-backed pools by default. They can be pinned to dedicated pool when flagged critical in the console. We'll add an opt-in tag for canaries that require priority.

DevOps Bot: [note] scheduled experiment: autoscaler-safety-margin-2026-03 will run in staging next Tue 03:00 UTC.

Mateo: testing plan: run 72h in staging with synthetic interrupt traces that mimic worst-case APAC bursts, measure p99/p95 latency, error rate, and cost delta. Also validate no oscillation under rapid spot returns.

Jin: edge cases — what if dedicated pool is exhausted? we should fall back to model-routing (lighter model variant) before failing requests.

Aisha Khan: yes — fallback chain: (1) try spot pool candidates, (2) provision dedicated in same region, (3) if dedicated exhausted, route low-priority traffic to smaller/quantized model variant, (4) last resort return graceful 503 with retry-after and telemetry hook.

Priya: telemetry — we need a new tag on traces: autoscaler_safety_decision={filled|fell_back|deferred} and include reason and chosen_pool_id.

Aisha Khan: agreed. Also add metric autoscaler.fallback_rate and autoscaler.safety_utilization.

Sam: ok looks good. I want the PR to include canary flags and a knob to set safety_margin_pct per service.

Aisha Khan: will do. I'll open a draft PR with config schema, algorithm pseudocode, and staging job. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Leo: thanks, Aisha. Ping when PR is up and I'll review the rollout/playbook.

DevOps Bot: [deploy] draft PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/789 (draft)

Aisha Khan: posted the PR. Leaving notes on cost sim and test plan in the description.

Mateo: ack — will run perf tests after staging run completes.
